papers.title: An Accurate and Efficient Approach to Knowledge Extraction from Scientific Publications Using Structured Ontology Models, Graph Neural Networks, and Large Language Models
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of biomedical literature makes it challenging for researchers to stay current. Integrating knowledge from various sources is crucial for studying complex biological systems. Traditional text-mining methods often have limited accuracy because they don’t capture semantic and contextual nuances. Deep-learning models can be computationally expensive and typically have low interpretability, though efforts in explainable AI aim to mitigate this. Furthermore, transformer-based models have a tendency to produce false or made-up information—a problem known as hallucination—which is especially prevalent in large language models (LLMs). This study proposes a hybrid approach combining text-mining techniques with graph neural networks (GNNs) and fine-tuned large language models (LLMs) to extend biomedical knowledge graphs and interpret predicted edges based on published literature. An LLM is used to validate predictions and provide explanations. Evaluated on a corpus of experimentally confirmed protein interactions, the approach achieved a Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 0.772. Applied to insomnia, the approach identified 25 interactions between 32 human proteins absent in known knowledge bases, including regulatory interactions between MAOA and 5-HT2C, binding between ADAM22 and 14-3-3 proteins, which is implicated in neurological diseases, and a circadian regulatory loop involving RORB and NR1D1. The hybrid GNN-LLM method analyzes biomedical literature efficiency to uncover potential molecular interactions for complex disorders. It can accelerate therapeutic target discovery by focusing expert verification on the most relevant automatically extracted information.

papers.title: Hierarchical Attentional Hybrid Neural Networks for Document Classification
papers.abstract: Document classification is a challenging task with important applications. The deep learning approaches to the problem have gained much attention recently. Despite the progress, the proposed models do not incorporate the knowledge of the document structure in the architecture efficiently and not take into account the contexting importance of words and sentences. In this paper, we propose a new approach based on a combination of convolutional neural networks, gated recurrent units, and attention mechanisms for document classification tasks. The main contribution of this work is the use of convolution layers to extract more meaningful, generalizable and abstract features by the hierarchical representation. The proposed method in this paper improves the results of the current attention-based approaches for document classification.

papers.title: Combining machine learning, simulations and experiments for improved glass design
papers.abstract: The design of novel glasses with tailored properties remains a grand challenge in materials science, traditionally requiring extensive trial-and-error experimentation. This talk presents a comprehensive framework that integrates machine learning, atomistic simulations, and targeted experiments to accelerate the discovery and optimization of glass compositions. We demonstrate how large-scale machine learning models trained on experimental databases can predict glass properties across nearly the entire periodic table, enabling rapid screening of promising compositions. These predictions are refined through physics-informed graph neural networks that capture atomic-scale interactions and energy conservation principles, providing deeper insights into structure-property relationships. The framework is enhanced by automated knowledge extraction from scientific literature using our materials-specific language model (MatSciBERT) and natural language processing techniques. We showcase practical applications including the development of radiation-resistant nuclear waste glasses, scratch-resistant display glasses, and specialty glasses for space applications. The talk concludes by highlighting how this integrated approach has led to the discovery of novel glass compositions with superior properties, validated through experimental synthesis and characterization. Our results demonstrate that the synergistic combination of artificial intelligence, computational modeling, and experimental validation can significantly accelerate the glass design process while reducing resource requirements and environmental impact.

papers.title: The Deep Arbitrary Polynomial Chaos Neural Network or how Deep Artificial Neural Networks could benefit from Data-Driven Homogeneous Chaos Theory
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence and Machine learning have been widely used in various fields of mathematical computing, physical modeling, computational science, communication science, and stochastic analysis. Approaches based on Deep Artificial Neural Networks (DANN) are very popular in our days. Depending on the learning task, the exact form of DANNs is determined via their multi-layer architecture, activation functions and the so-called loss function. However, for a majority of deep learning approaches based on DANNs, the kernel structure of neural signal processing remains the same, where the node response is encoded as a linear superposition of neural activity, while the non-linearity is triggered by the activation functions. In the current paper, we suggest to analyze the neural signal processing in DANNs from the point of view of homogeneous chaos theory as known from polynomial chaos expansion (PCE). From the PCE perspective, the (linear) response on each node of a DANN could be seen as a $1^{st}$ degree multi-variate polynomial of single neurons from the previous layer, i.e. linear weighted sum of monomials. From this point of view, the conventional DANN structure relies implicitly (but erroneously) on a Gaussian distribution of neural signals. Additionally, this view revels that by design DANNs do not necessarily fulfill any orthogonality or orthonormality condition for a majority of data-driven applications. Therefore, the prevailing handling of neural signals in DANNs could lead to redundant representation as any neural signal could contain some partial information from other neural signals. To tackle that challenge, we suggest to employ the data-driven generalization of PCE theory known as arbitrary polynomial chaos (aPC) to construct a corresponding multi-variate orthonormal representations on each node of a DANN to obtain Deep arbitrary polynomial chaos neural networks.

summary: The literature on Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for knowledge discovery in scientific literature reveals significant advancements in hybrid neural architectures that enhance knowledge extraction and document classification, particularly in biomedical contexts. However, challenges remain regarding computational efficiency, interpretability, and the effective utilization of document structure. Additionally, the integration of machine learning in materials science, such as glass design, showcases GNNs' predictive capabilities, indicating potential applications in literature-based knowledge extraction. Overall, there is a clear need for empirical studies validating GNN methodologies across diverse scientific domains to address existing gaps and improve knowledge discovery processes.
scholarly_positioning: While prior research has advanced the use of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) in knowledge extraction, particularly in biomedical literature, significant limitations persist regarding computational efficiency and the integration of document structure. Existing hybrid models often overlook the nuances of contextual information, leading to suboptimal performance in document classification tasks. Furthermore, the reliance on specific domains, such as biomedicine, restricts the generalizability of findings to broader scientific literature. This proposed research aims to empirically validate GNN methodologies across diverse domains, addressing these unresolved tensions and enhancing the interpretability and efficiency of knowledge discovery processes.
research_scope: This empirical study will investigate the application of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for knowledge extraction and document classification across diverse scientific domains, focusing on the integration of structured ontologies and attention mechanisms. The target population will include scientific literature datasets from biomedical and materials science fields, with a study period of six months for model training and evaluation. The GNN intervention will be compared against traditional neural networks and existing GNN models as baseline controls. Primary outcomes will include classification accuracy and computational efficiency, measured by F1 score and execution time, while secondary outcomes will assess interpretability scores. The study aims to address the limitations of current methodologies by validating the effectiveness of hybrid GNN architectures in enhancing knowledge discovery processes.

  "Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC)": "A measure of the quality of binary classifications, taking into account true and false positives and negatives, providing a balanced score even with imbalanced classes.",

  "Overfitting": "A modeling error that occurs when a model learns the training data too well, capturing noise and details that do not generalize to new data.",

technical_feasibility: The study requires access to labeled datasets from scientific literature, which may necessitate permissions for proprietary databases. It also requires GPU resources for training GNN models, as well as annotation protocols for data labeling. Since the research focuses on hybrid GNN architectures and their interpretability, access to open-source GNN models is essential for experimentation. If internal representations are to be analyzed, hidden-state access will be necessary. The study does not appear to require human participants or ethics approval unless user trust is explicitly evaluated. A feasible adjustment would be to ensure that the datasets used are publicly available or to collaborate with institutions that can provide access to necessary resources.
gap: Prior studies have demonstrated advancements in Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for knowledge extraction in biomedical literature; however, they treat the integration of document structure and contextual nuances as secondary, leaving unclear whether these factors significantly affect classification performance across diverse scientific domains. This matters theoretically because a deeper understanding of these integrations could enhance model interpretability and efficiency; therefore, this study investigates the empirical validation of hybrid GNN architectures that incorporate structured ontologies and attention mechanisms in knowledge discovery across various scientific fields.
question: How do hybrid Graph Neural Network architectures that integrate structured ontologies and attention mechanisms compare to traditional neural networks in improving classification accuracy and computational efficiency for knowledge extraction from diverse scientific literature datasets?
theoretical_mechanism: The proposed research investigates how hybrid Graph Neural Network (GNN) architectures, which integrate structured ontologies (independent variable) and attention mechanisms (mediator), affect classification accuracy and computational efficiency (dependent variables) in knowledge extraction from diverse scientific literature datasets. The theoretical framework is grounded in the notion that enhanced contextual understanding through structured ontologies and focused information processing via attention mechanisms can improve model performance. The causal chain suggests that the integration of these features leads to better representation of document structure, which subsequently enhances classification outcomes. System-level outcomes include improved classification accuracy and computational efficiency, while user-level outcomes may involve increased interpretability and trust in the model's predictions. Assumptions requiring empirical validation include the effectiveness of structured ontologies and attention mechanisms in diverse domains and their impact on model generalization across different scientific fields.
hypothesis: Hybrid Graph Neural Network architectures that integrate structured ontologies and attention mechanisms will demonstrate significantly higher classification accuracy compared to traditional neural networks in knowledge extraction from diverse scientific literature datasets, with improved computational efficiency as a mediating factor.

The proposed hybrid Graph Neural Network (GNN) architecture will be compared against traditional neural networks and existing GNN models as baseline controls. Key operationalized variables include classification accuracy, measured by F1 score and Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC), and computational efficiency, assessed through execution time. The evaluation will involve a fixed dataset size and consistent metrics to ensure reproducibility. Potential confounds, such as dataset quality and domain complexity, will be controlled by using standardized datasets and ensuring balanced representation across domains. phd_contribution_design: This research proposes a novel hybrid Graph Neural Network (GNN) architecture that integrates structured ontologies and attention mechanisms to enhance knowledge extraction from scientific literature. The mechanism-level claim posits that these integrations improve contextual understanding, leading to higher classification accuracy and computational efficiency. Existing literature fails to adequately address the impact of document structure and contextual nuances on GNN performance across diverse scientific domains. The falsifiable claim is that the proposed hybrid GNN will outperform traditional neural networks and existing GNN models in classification tasks, with empirical validation through F1 score and Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) as evidence. The strongest baseline for comparison will be traditional neural networks, while ablation studies will assess the individual contributions of structured ontologies and attention mechanisms. A negative or null result would suggest that these integrations do not significantly enhance model performance, challenging the theoretical framework and necessitating a reevaluation of the role of contextual features in GNNs.
pre_proposal_critique: The proposed contribution design may struggle to achieve an 85+ PhD-level score due to several critical weaknesses. First, the novelty claim lacks specificity; it must clearly articulate how the integration of structured ontologies and attention mechanisms uniquely enhances GNN performance compared to existing models, rather than merely asserting improvements. Second, the theoretical framework is underdeveloped; it should provide a more robust causal mechanism linking the proposed constructs to performance outcomes, supported by empirical evidence from prior studies. Lastly, the methodology is vague regarding baseline comparisons; it should specify the exact existing GNN models used as baselines and include comprehensive ablation studies to isolate the effects of each component, ensuring that the evaluation metrics are valid and applicable across diverse datasets. To address these objections, the proposal must refine its novelty claims, strengthen the theoretical underpinning with detailed causal pathways, and clarify the methodology with precise baseline definitions and ablation strategies.

proposal: This research proposal aims to empirically investigate the application of a novel hybrid Graph Neural Network (GNN) architecture that integrates structured ontologies and attention mechanisms for knowledge extraction and document classification across diverse scientific domains. The novelty of this approach lies in its explicit focus on enhancing contextual understanding and interpretability, which existing GNN models often overlook, particularly in their treatment of document structure and semantic nuances. Prior work, while advancing GNN methodologies in biomedical contexts, has not sufficiently addressed the generalizability of these models across other scientific literature, nor has it explored the specific contributions of structured ontologies and attention mechanisms in improving classification accuracy and computational efficiency. This study will operationalize constructs such as 'classification accuracy' (measured by F1 score and Matthews correlation coefficient) and 'computational efficiency' (assessed through execution time), ensuring clarity and reproducibility in methodology. The proposed methodology will include detailed baseline comparisons against traditional neural networks and existing GNN models, as well as comprehensive ablation studies to isolate the effects of each component. Data will be sourced from publicly available scientific literature datasets, ensuring a diverse representation of domains, while controls will be established through fixed dataset sizes and consistent evaluation metrics. The theoretical framework posits that the integration of structured ontologies will provide richer contextual embeddings, while attention mechanisms will enhance the model's focus on relevant features, leading to improved performance outcomes. This research addresses critical gaps in the literature by validating the effectiveness of hybrid GNN architectures in diverse scientific contexts, thereby advancing understanding of knowledge discovery processes and offering practical guidelines for their deployment in real-world applications.

The study will define core concepts such as GNNs, knowledge extraction, and document classification, ensuring clarity in the context of scientific literature. Technical feasibility is assumed based on access to labeled datasets from scientific literature and the availability of GPU resources for model training. The background highlights significant advancements in GNNs, particularly in biomedical contexts, while scholarly positioning underscores the limitations in computational efficiency and contextual integration in existing models. The literature reveals an empirical gap regarding the validation of GNN methodologies across various domains, leading to the research question: How do hybrid GNN architectures that integrate structured ontologies and attention mechanisms compare to traditional neural networks in improving classification accuracy and computational efficiency for knowledge extraction from diverse scientific literature datasets? The theoretical mechanism posits that enhanced contextual understanding through structured ontologies and focused processing via attention mechanisms will improve classification accuracy and computational efficiency, with system-level outcomes including improved performance metrics and user-level outcomes involving increased interpretability. The falsifiable hypothesis states that hybrid GNN architectures will demonstrate significantly higher classification accuracy compared to traditional neural networks, with improved computational efficiency as a mediating factor. Construct operationalization will include metrics such as F1 score and execution time, with a methodology that compares the proposed GNN architecture against traditional neural networks and existing GNN models as baselines, ensuring consistent evaluation metrics and controls. The PhD contribution design emphasizes the theoretical contribution of a new framework linking structured ontologies and attention mechanisms to GNN performance, while addressing pre-proposal reviewer concerns by clarifying the novelty claims, strengthening the theoretical framework, and specifying baseline comparisons. The expected contributions include theoretical, technical, empirical, and practical advancements in the field of knowledge discovery, emphasizing the novel integration of structured ontologies and attention mechanisms in GNNs. Key limitations include potential overfitting, generalization issues across domains, and the need for careful dataset management to mitigate biases.
